findings.title: Duplicate rows from non-idempotent load

facts.statement: Source keys are unique, so duplicates were introduced by the load

findings.hypothesis: A load was re-run in append mode, inserting part of a batch twice.
assumptions: The retry is the only re-run in the window
next_steps: Count duplicates by load batch/ingestion timestamp
Switch the load to MERGE on the primary key

findings.title: Source rows dropped by transform

facts.statement: All missing rows have quantity between -3 and -1

findings.hypothesis: The filter `quantity > 0` in the transform removes these rows.
assumptions: The dropped rows are valid business records (e.g. refunds)
next_steps: Confirm with the data owner whether these rows should be excluded
If not, remove or narrow the filter and backfill

findings.title: NULL customer_id in target

facts.statement: customer_id is taken from a LEFT JOIN to warehouse.dim_customer
Context records a change to dim_customer
Context records a change to dim_customer

findings.hypothesis: A key change in dim_customer breaks the join, so unmatched rows get NULL customer_id.
assumptions: Missing values are not present upstream
next_steps: Query unmatched customer_id values against the dimension
Update the join to the new key format or add a mapping table

findings.title: revenue mismatch

facts.statement: All mismatched rows have currency = EUR
Transform has special handling when currency = 'EUR'

findings.hypothesis: The transform converts revenue for EUR rows, but source revenue is already converted (double conversion).
assumptions: The rate used equals the observed ratio
next_steps: Compare revenue for a few EUR orders at each pipeline stage
Remove the duplicate conversion and reprocess affected dates

summary: Heuristic analysis matched 4 known failure patterns.
